claim: Accepted evidence changes future search behaviour; rejected evidence cannot. Both halves are one claim.
fixture: Reuse the tiny graph-based OPT-6 fixture. Two eligible transitions are predetermined: A compiles all seven eligible layer-0 projections; B compiles only layer-0 q_proj. Layer 1 remains at source precision. Compile and independently establish both candidates without feeding a MeasurementKey into their writers.
positive: Deserialize S0; show exactly two eligible experiments and selection A. Derive PreparedExperiment from S0, dispatch its request through ExecutorRegistry and DeclaredArtifacts to a deterministic fixture executor, capture independently read candidate authority, serialize MeasurementArtifact and ingest through ingest_bytes. Exactly one observation changes SearchFacts. The next selection must be predetermined B, with A explicitly pruned as AlreadyObserved. Deserialize S1 and reproduce B. Replay the accepted artifact: no second write and B stays selected.
negative: Start again from the exact same serialized S0. Dispatch A through the same executor path, but return an incomplete run-validity report and freshly seal it. Ingestion must refuse with IncompleteRun. Compare the whole snapshot, serialized bytes, frontier and promotion outputs; the next selection and prepared request must remain A. Also supply independently valid candidate Y for authorised A and require the same scientific noninterference after identity refusal.
anti_cheat: No direct MeasurementRegistry writes, fixture-record helpers, manual applied-action changes, replacement ranking rules or injected post-measurement choices. Expected B is identified before any observation is accepted. Assert concrete experiment keys and pruning reason rather than merely asserting a nonempty registry or a different next result.
limits: The executor is an explicitly synthetic deterministic observation provider over real persisted input artifacts. This witnesses control-plane composition and non-repetition of an accepted experiment; it does not demonstrate numerical kernel correctness, quality-dependent promotion, K3 execution or historical pointer-attribution replay. Those are not added to the claim after seeing the result.
sequencing: Implement only on a fresh branch from merged Transition B. Register EXECUTION-EVIDENCE-SCOPE-1 separately; it does not block this internally consistent tiny fixture. No K3 run in this change.
